original_question: What gene on chromosome 10 encodes the human enzyme Heparanase-2 and is linked to an autosomal recessive disorder causing children to appear as if they are crying when they smile?

final_qi.question: What gene on chromosome 10 encodes the human enzyme Heparanase-2 and is linked to an autosomal recessive disorder causing children to appear as if they are crying when they smile?
final_qi.long_answer: Heparanase-2 is encoded by the HPSE2 gene located on chromosome 10q23-q24. Homozygous loss-of-function mutations in HPSE2 cause autosomal-recessive urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome, in which affected children have a characteristic grimace that makes them look as if they are crying when they attempt to smile.

final_answer.long_answer: The HPSE2 gene, located on chromosome 10q23-q24, encodes the human protein Heparanase-2. Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in HPSE2 cause urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome, an autosomal recessive disorder in which affected children exhibit a characteristic inverted facial expression—appearing to cry when they attempt to smile—along with congenital bladder dysfunction.
